result.document_summary: Boston city FAQ for tenants explaining the Housing Stability Notification Act ordinance, which requires landlords to give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources (and copy the city) when ending a tenancy.
result.notes: The HSNA is a notice-and-procedure ordinance tied to eviction/non-renewal; it does not set allowed eviction causes, so it is recorded as a procedural just-cause-eviction-category rule with moderate confidence. The document states a specific citation only as 'Sec. 10-11.7' of City of Boston Ordinances.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act - notice of tenants' rights and city notification
rules.requirement: A landlord or foreclosing owner ending a tenancy or declining to renew a lease must deliver a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the Notice to Quit and send a copy of the Notice to Quit or non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. The requirements cannot be waived, and violations are ticketed (warning, then $300 per day) but do not halt the eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with the Notice to Quit; copy to Office of Housing Stability
rules.citation: City of Boston Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.quoted_span:
The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.
rules.coverage_text: All landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a residential unit in the City of Boston.
